- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, it often overcorrects; cap the downward slope to avoid overshoot.
- If true price moves >10% from recent mean within 3–5 days, model underreacts; adjust forecast to align with mean reversion trend.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts rise, it often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment turns neutral or bullish.
- Model tends to underestimate late-period price increases (last 7–10 days) when sentiment is bullish; add 2–5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment >0.6.
- If model forecast is below 65% of recent 5-day average, and sentiment is neutral or bullish, increase forecast by 3–5% to avoid underestimation.
- Avoid forecasting sharp declines after recent spikes unless sentiment is clearly bearish (≥0.8); model often overreacts to sentiment shifts.
